title: Solve-x attention and responsive exemplar

sourceRefs.summary: Run-contract target that explains why this generated contract exists.
Accepted exemplar sequence, attention problem, and phone-specific projection constraint.
Observed review occlusion, moving-native fade, overflow concerns, and open human checkpoint.

verification: focused unit and Playwright checks for each slice
allowedWork: Solve-x reader, semantic lesson document, authoring, static compiler, hydration metadata, attention projection, accessible controls, responsive presentation, equation material ownership, reader-specific developer review placement, focused tests, deterministic captures, and durable evidence.

Preserve the existing searchable transcript, static and no-JavaScript output, semantic math and lineage, KaTeX identity and metrics, exact URLs, direct seek, rewind, review history, and production exclusion.
disallowedWork: Do not implement or promote distribution, fractions, radicals, exponents, function wrapping, calculus, linear algebra, code, graphs, WebGL, providers, or other animation families.

Do not generalize the optional attention schema or solve-x visual recipes before final human approval; do not build arbitrary text, KaTeX, or code overflow infrastructure; do not add public review tooling.
goal: Perfect solve-x as the single attention-responsive exemplar with non-occluding developer review, solid native handoff, phased prose-to-motion attention, wide stable-island scrollytelling, and a narrow focus stepper; stop for human approval before any family promotion.
commitCadence: Commit after each independently verified reversible slice with its Theseus evidence.
stopConditions: Stop immediately if semantic math or lineage, searchable prose, static output, URL restoration, seek or rewind authority, KaTeX identity or font metrics, review history, accessibility, or production exclusion regresses.
Stop at a visual checkpoint if review placement, native handoff, attention ownership, or phone clarity remains ambiguous; retain the smallest exemplar rollback unit.
Stop if implementation requires family-wide promotion, arbitrary overflow infrastructure, public review infrastructure, or scope outside the approved solve-x exemplar.
Stop after the final human exemplar checkpoint and do not promote the pattern without explicit approval.

slices.title: Close_prior_checkpoint
slices.summary: Closed the predecessor only after its human checkpoint was performed and explicitly recorded as not accepted; preserved its history and no-generalization outcome.

slices.title: Create_successor_contract
slices.summary: Created the exact approved 25-slice solve-x-only run contract with broad verification, per-slice commits, preserved fallback projection, four visual stop gates, and explicit exclusions for family promotion and general overflow.

slices.title: Desktop_failure_baseline
slices.summary: Added a repeatable desktop/phone baseline harness. At 1280x900 and progress 833, the open 360x413 review panel overlaps 60,131.625 square pixels of the 509x558 animation stage without changing scroll or semantic progress; the capture visibly obscures the active equation.

slices.title: Phone_failure_baseline
slices.summary: At 390x844 and progress 833, the sticky 362x309 stage covers the active heading by 174px while the next heading appears far below, so text and the relevant motion cannot be read together. The open review panel occupies the lower 413px; both behaviors are now captured by the repeatable baseline.

slices.title: Review_placement_policy
slices.summary: Added a pure, validated placement policy tied to the reader's existing 881px two-column boundary: semantic readers choose left-prose-rail when wide and captured-moment-sheet when narrow, while every other review consumer retains bottom-right. Three focused laws and repository typecheck pass.

slices.title: Wide_review_dock
slices.summary: Mounted semantic-reader review with an explicit left-prose-rail placement at the wide breakpoint. At 1280x900 the open panel moved from x=902 to x=18 and animation-stage overlap fell from 60,131.625px2 to zero, while scroll, semantic progress, focus restoration, generic-shell behavior, type safety, and production exclusion remained unchanged.

slices.title: Narrow_review_flow
slices.summary: Added a live responsive semantic-reader review projection. Below 881px, opening review creates one bounded lower sheet, locks the current semantic moment immediately, leaves the 390x844 equation stage unobscured, and returns to the prose rail on resize; hidden state, focus, scroll, progress, review history, and production exclusion remain intact.

slices.title: Review_visual_checkpoint
slices.summary: Accepted the review-placement visual stop gate after inspecting the six-state contact sheet and open-review desktop/phone captures. Review chrome no longer occludes the equation, open and closed ownership is singular, and phone lesson compression remains isolated for the later responsive-projection slices.

slices.title: Handoff_instrumentation
slices.summary: Added a repeatable 33-frame live solve-x handoff sampler covering every transformation seam with native/material opacity and bounding geometry. It proves the perceived fade is the current 8% smooth-crossfade policy: matching DOM owners coexist at partial opacity even though endpoint geometry is sound.

slices.title: Solid_material_handoff_law
slices.summary: Added and verified an opt-in atomic-v1 native/material handoff. It assigns each persistent visual frame to exactly one solid owner, handles one-sided arrival and retirement at exact endpoints, and preserves crossfade-v1 as the compatibility default until the solve-x exemplar explicitly selects atomic ownership.

slices.title: Solve-x_ownership_repair
slices.summary: Selected atomic-v1 in linear-solve asset metadata, inferred it through the typed presentation profile, and threaded it into reader symbol motion. Live solve-x owner/native opacity is now exactly zero or one at all sampled seams, while other assets keep crossfade-v1 and semantic/cross-surface parity remains intact.

slices.title: Handoff_rewind_gate
slices.summary: Added a dense browser gate across both solve-x seams. Forward and reverse scroll, reload, and direct URL seek now prove identical owner geometry and fragment poses by semantic identity, exact atomic opacity, stable URL progress, and correct rewind direction; DOM insertion order is intentionally excluded from semantic authority.

slices.title: Handoff_visual_checkpoint
slices.summary: Accepted the atomic handoff visual stop gate after inspecting sixteen seam captures and the canonical contact sheet. Equation ink remains solid with stable KaTeX metrics and no duplicate ghost, dimming ramp, font swap, or endpoint jump; prose attention behavior remains explicitly separate.

slices.title: Attention_phase_schema
slices.summary: Added the optional phased-attention-v1 story sidecar with orient/act/settle/inspect phase kinds and stable phase, beat, checkpoint, global progress, cue, and semantic focus identities. Canonical beat prose remains the searchable source; existing lessons and runtime behavior are unchanged.

slices.title: Attention_authoring_validation
slices.summary: Extended inference-friendly lesson authoring and Markdown parsing for phased attention, added strict cycle/coverage/identity/focus validation and semantic reference resolution, and authored the canonical solve-x lesson with three complete orient-act-settle-inspect cycles over progress 0-1000. No other lesson opts in.

slices.title: Attention_projector
slices.summary: Added a pure optional attention projector with exact semantic progress, gaze targets, reversible phase selection, and hold-play-hold visual remapping.
